title: hx-swap: innerHTML, outerHTML, beforebegin, afterend, and delete Strategies

progressiveExplaining.eli5: When the server sends you a new puzzle piece, `hx-swap` tells the browser where to put it: empty the box and put it inside (`innerHTML`), replace the box itself (`outerHTML`), slide it just before the box (`beforebegin`), slide it right after the box (`afterend`), or throw the box in the trash (`delete`).
progressiveExplaining.junior: `hx-swap` controls how the returned HTML response is placed into the DOM relative to `hx-target`. Default is `innerHTML` (replaces children). Common strategies: `outerHTML` (replaces target element itself), `beforebegin` (inserts before target), `afterbegin` (prepends inside target), `beforeend` (appends inside target), `afterend` (inserts after target), and `delete` (removes target). You can also control scroll behavior via `hx-swap="innerHTML scroll:top"`.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `hx-swap` maps directly to the DOM's `insertAdjacentHTML` and `outerHTML` APIs, combined with transition timing modifiers. Modifiers like `swap:300ms` and `settle:300ms` coordinate with CSS transition classes (`.htmx-swapping`, `.htmx-settling`), enabling smooth exit and enter animations during DOM replacement without custom JavaScript animation libraries.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: When the response arrives, HTMX runs the swap lifecycle: (1) adds `.htmx-swapping` to the target, (2) waits for the `swap` delay timer, (3) executes the chosen strategy using native DOM primitives (`insertAdjacentHTML`, `replaceChild`, `remove`), (4) adds `.htmx-settling` to new content, and (5) removes settling classes after the settle delay, firing `htmx:afterSettle`.

interviewGotchas.question: What is the difference between `hx-swap="outerHTML"` and `hx-swap="innerHTML"`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your precision with DOM element replacement boundaries.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `innerHTML` replaces the *children* of the target element while keeping the target element's opening and closing tag intact. `outerHTML` replaces the *target element itself* along with its children, substituting it entirely with the incoming HTML response.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: If using `hx-swap="outerHTML"`, the incoming server response must include the outer container element (with attributes and IDs) if subsequent HTMX interactions on that element are expected.

interviewGotchas.question: How do you animate element deletion with `hx-swap="delete"`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks understanding of HTMX CSS transition swap timing modifiers.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Use the `swap` timing modifier: `hx-swap="delete swap:500ms"`. When triggered, HTMX adds the `.htmx-swapping` CSS class to the element, waits 500ms (allowing a CSS `opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.8)` transition to play), and then removes the element from the DOM.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Without specifying `swap:500ms`, `hx-swap="delete"` removes the element instantly, preventing any CSS exit transitions from playing.
